text.p: Following are the main stories in Monday's Malaysian newspapers. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

-- Malaysia will agree to any solution by the Peruvian government that will ensure the safety of its ambassador who is among the more than 300 hostages being held at the Japanese ambassador's residence in Lima. Prime Minister Mahathir Mohamad said Peruvian President Alberto Fujimori's statement that he would not use force against the rebels if they surrendered their arms and freed all captives "may be one way to solve the crisis".

-- The Malaysian government is negotiating for more landing rights in India for Malaysia Airlines to cope with the increasing air traffic flow between the two countries, Prime Minister Mahathir Mohamad said.

-- Prime Minister Mahathir said he wanted the practice of signing memoranda of understanding (MOU) to be repalced with actual agreements. He said many MOU which Malaysian entrepreneurs had signed locally and abroad in the past had not materialised, making the events meaningless.

-- The United Malays National Organisation's youth wing wants the Australian government to be more pro-active in dealing with the anti-Asian sentiment spread by its member of parliament, Pauline Hanson. Its vice-chairman Hishamuddin Hussein said they should not just acknowledge the issue without taking appropriate measures to curb the racist sentiments.
